newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Oil giant Shell to review Singapore operations.
newsitem.headline: Oil giant Shell to review Singapore operations.

text.p: Despite better than expected conditions in its oil product export markets in 1996, Anglo-Dutch oil giant Shell is reviewing Singapore manufacturing, supply and trading (MST) operations to meet growing competition, chairman of the Shell companies in Singapore, Tim Faithfull, said in a company newsletter.

"As part of our efforts to grow the margin of our business, we will be reviewing the full range of our MST activities and processes to ... link them to our customers better ... and also support the developing regional MST structure," Faithfull said.
But at the same time, the year 1996 was one of strong co-operation with regional and inter-regional affiliates, he said.

"SIETCO's (Shell International Eastern Trading Co) close links with STASCO (London) were further strengthened by the formation of a global "Joint Book" now covering the full range of traded products," he said.

Trading and supply co-operation was further deepened with the formation of the South East Asia Forum and the Operations Forum, comprising companies from Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines, while the North East Asia Trading Strategy
"At the same time, we will be examining our cost base in each function, benchmarking our activites and developing options that will improve our bottom line," he said.

Faithfull said Shell's oil product exports last year benefitted from a combination of events such as weather conditions, growing ASEAN demand, strong Chinese buying in the fourth quarter, the delay in the start-up of new refining capacity in South Korea and low stock levels in main consuming areas in the West.
Group aims to optimise overall Shell trading activities.
